prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: reusable BLANK CHARACTER POSE TEMPLATE for 2D game sprite-sheet generation.
Edit the attached Gardener sprite sheet into a neutral pose/layout reference. Preserve its 4 COLUMN by 4 ROW regular square-cell organization and the same elevated north-up orthographic camera, walking gestures, centered placement and generous separation.
Replace EVERY character with the SAME blank matte light-gray human mannequin: a simple smooth head, featureless face (tiny nose projection permitted only to distinguish facing), plain torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. No hat, hair, scarf, coat, bag, costume details, gender cues, jewelry, shadows, colors or text. The mannequin is a pose guide that any character can be painted over.
EXACT layout: sixteen figures total, one in each equal square cell. ROW 1 faces DOWN toward the viewer. ROW 2 faces UP away from viewer. ROW 3 faces LEFT (nose and toes point to the LEFT edge of the image). ROW 4 faces RIGHT (nose and toes point to RIGHT edge). Do not put two right-facing rows.
Columns show one consistent four-frame walk family: 1 neutral/idle, 2 left foot forward with opposite arm, 3 feet passing/near-neutral, 4 right foot forward with opposite arm. Side views must clearly alternate the forward foot. All have same body size and proportions. Both soles remain within their own cell. In each cell, centered at 50% width, head near 13% height, lowest grounded sole near 87% height. Keep about 13% top and bottom clear margins and at least 18% horizontal clear margins. Simplified game proportions similar to the source, not realistic anatomical diagrams.
Output a square transparent RGBA PNG with only the sixteen gray mannequins; no visible grid lines, foot lines, letters, numbers, titles or checkerboard. No source Gardener identity remains.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: reusable blank 4x4 character sprite layout template.
Edit this gray mannequin template. Preserve the exact 4x4 equal-cell layout, head/body proportions, size, positions, row directions and camera. Row1 front/down, row2 back/up, row3 LEFT, row4 RIGHT.
Make only these repairs:
1. Remove all white edge flecks and floating pixels. Clean gray silhouettes with true transparent background.
2. Make the fourth pose in EACH row the OPPOSITE walk step from the second pose. The template currently repeats the second pose in column4; fix that. Front/back: swap which leg is extended and which arm swings forward. Side-left row: column2 visible near arm swings BACK toward image RIGHT, near leg swings FORWARD toward image LEFT; column4 visible near arm swings FORWARD toward image LEFT and near leg swings BACK toward image RIGHT. Side-right row: column2 near arm FORWARD toward image RIGHT and near leg BACK toward image LEFT; column4 near arm BACK toward image LEFT and near leg FORWARD toward image RIGHT. Keep torso and head location invariant. Use a slightly darker gray on FAR limbs so opposite foot phases can be distinguished; near limbs light gray.
No character identity, clothing, hair, accessories, floor, shadow, visible grid, checkerboard, text, label or watermark. Output sixteen clean matte-gray mannequins only on genuine transparency.

Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: production 2D game character sprite sheet, 4 columns by 4 rows, transparent RGBA.
Input images: IMAGE 1 is the blank sixteen-pose layout template and is the PRIMARY SPATIAL AUTHORITY. IMAGE 2 is Mara's canonical identity and clothes. IMAGE 3 is the Gardener sheet for painted game-art STYLE ONLY, not identity.
Dress/replace every gray mannequin in image 1 with the SAME Mara from image 2: young adult farmer woman, copper-auburn hair in a loose practical bun with side wisps, hazel eyes, freckles, muted brick-red kerchief knotted at her left side, olive-green rolled-sleeve shirt, brown full-length bib overalls with small brass buckles, brown work boots. No hat, dress, apron or bag. Translate her identity into charming softly painted gouache miniature game art matching image 3; keep her adult identity legible with a large head and compact body. No pixel-art texture.
Preserve the template's regular 4x4 grid, elevated orthographic camera, centered positions, identical scale, full-body framing and sixteen figures. Each equal cell contains exactly one figure, never overlap cells. Row 1 faces DOWN toward viewer; row 2 faces UP away; row 3 faces LEFT, nose and toes toward LEFT image edge; row 4 faces RIGHT, nose and toes toward RIGHT edge.
Columns: 1 idle/feet together; 2 LEFT leg steps forward, right arm forward; 3 passing/feet near together; 4 RIGHT leg steps forward, left arm forward. Correct the template's repeated step pose: columns 2 and 4 must exchange near/far legs and opposite arms visibly, not repeat the same step. Do not change facing across a row. Same head size, hair, clothing and body proportions in every cell. Match overall template size, foot grounding and generous clear margins.
Clean silhouette cutouts on true transparency. Remove ALL template white flecks, halos, scattered pixels, mannequin remnants and shadows. No floor, checkerboard, grid, labels, text, border, watermark or extra objects. Soft directional painting light shared by all figures, no glow. The output is ONLY the finished 4x4 Mara sheet.

Transform the referenced Gardener sprite sheet into a reusable pose template with NO character identity. Keep the sixteen cell positions, camera, compact head/body proportions and down/up/left/right row order. Replace all characters by blank smooth gray mannequins on a perfectly opaque warm ivory background. No hat, hair, clothes, scarf, face, bag or other identity. row1 FRONT/DOWN, row2 BACK/UP, row3 profile LEFT, row4 profile RIGHT.

Clean flat illustrated forms, simple dark outlines, no texture, no specks, no grid or annotations, no shadows, no labels, no checkerboard. All heads same size and centered in cells. Preserve generous gutters. Entire soles visible in every cell. All sixteen figures have exactly one head, two arms, two legs. This image is a pose guide, not final game art.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: game-ready 4x4 RGBA sprite atlas with STRICT EMPTY GUTTERS.
Edit this Mara walk sheet. The art and walk poses are good; the figures are TOO TALL and cross the equal row boundaries when sliced into a regular 4x4 grid. Correct ONLY the layout/scale.
Shrink EVERY figure to 72 percent of its current size, keeping its painting and pose intact. Put each smaller full-body figure in the exact center of its own equal square cell of an evenly spaced 4 COLUMN by 4 ROW grid. Cell center positions are x=12.5%,37.5%,62.5%,87.5% of full image width and y=12.5%,37.5%,62.5%,87.5% of full image height. Keep the feet of each row at 82% of EACH CELL height. Every individual figure is at most 68% of cell height including its hair and boots, leaving at least 14% empty transparent margin above AND below it in EVERY cell. Do not fill the available cell area. We intentionally need smaller figures with MUCH MORE empty space; the game scales them at import.
Preserve all sixteen poses, their row order (front, back, left, right) and column order (idle, step1, passing, step2). Preserve identity, proportions, clothing, hair, colors and lighting. No mirroring/reordering poses. Do not add shadows, reflections, specks, grid lines, text or labels. Only the 16 smaller sprites with generous fully transparent gutters on a square RGBA canvas.
